Pulse for 12 October 2026

The stories from 12 October 2026 in the Pulse of the Sapaude app, in our own words. Terms you don’t know are explained in the glossary. Glossary

New model

Big vision AI on your phone

A multimodal model reads images and video as well as text, and OpenBMB says its new open MiniCPM-V 4.7 family can do that on a phone, including a large mixture-of-experts variant.

New model

Meta agents remember more

An AI agent is a model that can keep working on a goal across steps and tools, and Meta says its new Muse Wonder models are built for exactly that kind of personal and work help.

Device

Servers built for AI agents

AMD's new Helion is an open blueprint for data-center server racks designed around AI agents, which spend much of their time on ordinary processors rather than graphics chips.

New model

Legal AI checks contracts

Z.ai's new GLM-Legal is an AI model trained specifically for legal work like contract review, and it shows why specialist models are on the rise.

Device

Microsoft AI on own chips

An AI chip is specialized hardware that runs AI models, and Microsoft says its own Maia chips already power Copilot and will become its main way to answer AI requests.

Everyday tool

AI worlds now have sound

A world model is an AI that builds a scene you can move through, and Helix World is a free demo that also generates stereo sound that turns when you look around.

Study

AI solves old math puzzles

A proof is a step-by-step argument that a math claim is true, and Google DeepMind's AlphaProof Nexus solved open problems and got those results peer-reviewed in the journal Science, according to The Decoder.
